title: Homeschool notice of intent: find the right filing
dek: Find the correct homeschool notice, recipient and filing order, then keep proof of submission without confusing notice with school withdrawal.
metaDescription: Find the correct homeschool notice, recipient and filing order, then keep proof of submission without confusing notice with school withdrawal.

paragraphs: A homeschool notice of intent tells the responsible authority that you are establishing a home education program. Whether you need one, where it goes, when to send it and whether acknowledgement must come before withdrawal depend on your state and your chosen legal route. Do not copy another family's filing sequence without checking those details.

The difficult moment is often not filling in the form. It is deciding whether you can stop sending your child to their current school on Monday. This US guide helps you identify the correct paperwork and ask a precise question about that transition. It does not establish your eligibility or replace state-specific legal advice.

body.heading: Three documents with different jobs
rows: Registers or notifies the home education arrangement.
Correct authority, required contents, timing and renewal.
Ends enrollment at the current school.
Permitted effective date and school process.
Recipient, delivery method and what records are available.

body.heading: Start with the legal route, not a downloaded letter
paragraphs: An online public school, a private umbrella arrangement and a parent-directed home education program may have different procedures. First identify what you are actually starting. Then use the current state education or responsible nonpublic-education agency page and the law it links to. A district form can be useful, but distinguish legally required information from optional requests.

Florida provides one concrete example: its [home education statute](https://leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=1000-1099/1002/Sections/1002.41.html) requires a signed written notice to the district superintendent within 30 days of establishing the program, identifying enrolled children by full legal name, address and birthdate. That is a Florida home education rule, not permission to wait 30 days anywhere else.

North Carolina illustrates why the order matters. Its [opening guidance](https://www.doa.nc.gov/divisions/non-public-education/home-schools/faqs/opening-closing-reopening) says an enrolled child should continue attending until home school registration is complete. It also describes one notice for the household, rather than a separate annual notice for every child. Neither example can be substituted for your own route.

body.heading: Before you submit anything
items: Write the state, county or district, child's age and legal education route at the top of your notes. Age and enrollment status can change the process.
Locate the current official instructions and record the page address and date you read it. Follow its link to the applicable law where provided.
Copy the exact recipient, permitted submission method, required information and deadline. Identify whether a household or an individual child is registered.
Check the sequence explicitly: submission, acknowledgement or approval if applicable, withdrawal, and the first instructional day. Do not treat those as interchangeable.
Ask whether you need a new filing after a move, another child, a program change or the next school year. Put each confirmed trigger in your calendar.
Keep the completed submission and its receipt together. A blank form, a draft email and a successful portal submission are three different records.

body.heading: Ask a question someone can answer

items.line: My child is currently enrolled and we want to establish a home education program under this route. What must be submitted or acknowledged before withdrawal, and where is that sequence published?

items.situation: A form asks for more than the instructions
items.line: Could you identify which fields are required under the applicable rule and which are optional? I want to submit the correct notice and keep a complete record.

body.heading: Example: a start date that changes
paragraphs: Invented example: Jordan plans a Friday withdrawal and a Monday home education start. On Tuesday, Jordan learns that the applicable registration process must be completed first. The family keeps the existing enrollment in place while confirming the sequence, saves the acknowledgement when it arrives, and agrees the withdrawal date with the school. The planned Monday date moves; the records show what actually happened.

The useful record is not a confident-looking letter dated before everything was ready. It is a short chain: instruction checked, notice submitted, acknowledgement retained where required, withdrawal confirmed, teaching begun. Keep each item with its actual date. Do not backdate a missing filing to make the sequence look complete.

body.heading: If you have already started or received conflicting advice
paragraphs: If you may have missed a required filing, contact the responsible office promptly with factual dates. Ask how to correct the record and whether any additional action is required. An unanswered search, a neighbor's experience or an informal assurance cannot establish that no notice is needed.

If there is a truancy warning, an existing custody order, a dispute about which state governs, or disagreement between official instructions and a demand you received, get state-specific help from legal aid or an education attorney. Keep the written notice and response deadline. Do not let a general organizing checklist delay a response.

items.q: Is a notice of intent the same as withdrawing from school?
items.a: No. The notice concerns the home education arrangement; withdrawal concerns existing enrollment. They may go to different offices and may have a required order. Ask both the responsible home education authority and the current school how the transition should be documented before setting the final attendance date.

items.q: Can I write my own notice instead of using a form?
items.a: Possibly, but it depends on the applicable rule. Some routes specify required information without requiring a particular template; others use a portal or prescribed form. Check the official instructions before substituting a letter. Keep a copy of exactly what you submitted, not just a reusable template.

items.q: Do I submit a notice every year?
items.a: There is no national annual filing rule. Confirm whether your arrangement requires one initial notice, annual renewal, or updates after particular changes. Record the trigger as well as the date. A continuing registration does not necessarily remove separate testing, evaluation, instruction or record-keeping duties.
